target_customer: UAE consumers and small businesses and freelancers who accept payments through links and messaging apps
problem: People and small businesses in the UAE lacked easy peer to peer and online payments; Ziina offers a wallet, payment links and a gateway.
business_model: Payments take rate on transactions plus paid membership (Violet) and card interchange
product_category: Digital wallet and payments in the Middle East

founders.name: Faisal Toukan
founders.background_notes: YC page: experience in consumer fintech, enterprise sales, blockchain, startups and venture capital.

founders.name: Sarah Toukan
education: Stanford, BS and MS in Mechanical Engineering
founders.background_notes: YC page: product experience in UAE fintech, London proptech and Silicon Valley autonomous vehicles.

founders.name: Andrew Gold
founders.background_notes: Moved from San Francisco to Dubai to found Ziina per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: A wallet app with payments and compliance is standard engineering, but licensing and banking partnerships were the hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: It became the first venture backed startup to get a UAE Central Bank Stored Value Facility license (August 2024 per its site headlines), and peer to peer use has network effects.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; Ziina kept growing as an independent licensed company.

market_need_then: Gulf News in 2021 described a banked and unbanked UAE where residents lacked easy digital transfers, and Ziina launched its app in June 2020 per founder quote.

identity.visual_style: modern fintech app screens; a Dribbble case study covers the branding

branding.brand_signature: ZiiBoard payment keyboard inside WhatsApp and Instagram chats
branding.community_and_virality: Product line extensions named with Zii prefix (ZiiBoard, ZiiLink, ZiiCard) build a consistent family of names.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive coined name with a product naming system and regional press coverage, though evidence of consumer virality is thin.

outcome_analysis: Ziina launched in the UAE in 2020, joined YC in Winter 2021 and grew to 57 people. It raised a 22 million dollar Series A in September 2024 led by Altos, reported by several outlets, and won a Central Bank license. Success rests on a regulated position in a fast growing payments market and a team with fintech and engineering experience.
notes: Series A reported by Finextra, Wamda and FinTech Futures (search results; Wamda and the pages were not opened because of fetch limits). An 850K pre-seed led by Class 5 Global and a 7.5M seed led by Avenir appear only in one profile and are unverified, not recorded as rounds; the 'above 30 million total' claim is likewise unverified. The competitor search returned undated lists (PayTabs, Telr, Tabby, Mamo Pay), so none are recorded as of founding.
